preamble: Click insertion in an inherited Nguni word. Wiktionary derives Zulu -qamela 'lean on, rest the head' and umqamelo 'pillow, headrest' (q = postalveolar click [ǃ]) from Proto-Bantu *-kɪ́gamɪda, applicative of *-kɪ́gama. The Northern Sotho cognates sama and mosamelo have no click. The source does not state the mechanism. This is a sporadic, lexically specific replacement within the wider adoption of Khoisan clicks into Nguni, which has been argued to have been helped by hlonipha avoidance speech (Sands & Gunnink 2019; Gunnink 2023); it is not a regular sound change. Only one root is attested (the verb and its derived noun), so certainty is 2.

examples.note: Derived from the same root, so not independent evidence. Compare Northern Sotho mosamelo.

sources: Herbert, R. K. (1990). Hlonipha and the ambiguous woman. Anthropos 85, 455–473 (cited in Wikipedia: Avoidance speech).
